CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ashley is a 14-year-old previously healthy female who developed acute onset right-sided abdominal pain severe enough to cause her to bend over. Initial evaluation was attributed to gastroenteritis and treated supportively, but symptoms worsened the following day. Subsequent ultrasound revealed unequal kidney sizes. Evaluation in Jacksonville confirmed the right kidney was not functioning and was atrophic. Imaging also showed cysts on kidney and ovaries, swollen lymph nodes, and infection. She received treatment in Atlanta over 4 days with improvement in vomiting. She continues to complain of abdominal pain and burning sensation, particularly with eating and certain beverages. She reports dysuria (burning with urination), especially after carbonated drinks, and occasional difficulty initiating urination. Denies hematuria. Parent reports Ashley likely had a severe infection in childhood that affected her kidney. At age 4, she was hospitalized 3-4 times over several months with fevers and symptoms, treated with fluids and antibiotics, which eventually resolved. Pregnancy and delivery were uncomplicated.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive: Abdominal pain, burning sensation (especially with eating), dysuria (particularly after carbonated drinks), difficulty initiating urination.
Negative: Hematuria.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Recurrent febrile hospitalizations (3-4 times over several months) at age 4 treated with fluids and antibiotics.

MEDICATIONS
Pepcid 40 mg daily.
Claritin for allergies.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Paternal grandfather: Posterior urethral valves, obstructive neuropathy, chronic kidney disease, dialysis-dependent, renal transplant (subsequently failed), died at age 47.
Paternal great-aunt: End-stage renal disease, chronic kidney disease stage 5, diabetes, hypertension.
Paternal relatives (cousins): Kidney disease.
Maternal grandmother: Breast cancer.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays softball and interested in joining drill team over summer. Active lifestyle.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing female, alert and oriented, sitting comfortably without acute distress.
Lungs: Sound great.
Heart: Sound great.
Otherwise: Within normal limits.

RESULTS
Renal ultrasound: Right kidney atrophic; left kidney enlarged.
Kidney function: Good.
Blood pressure: Good.
Prior imaging (Jacksonville): Cysts on kidney and ovaries, swollen lymph nodes, infection noted.
Genetic panel: No clinically significant mutations identified.
Gastroenterology evaluation: No clinically significant findings.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
14-year-old female with atrophic right kidney likely secondary to severe childhood infection. Current kidney function is good and blood pressure is normal. Right kidney is small, causing left kidney to work harder; this will be monitored but requires no intervention at this time. Patient at increased risk for future development of hypertension and proteinuria.

Plan:
1. Annual monitoring including renal ultrasound to monitor kidney size and function, urinalysis to assess for protein and blood, and blood pressure check.
2. Avoid NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen); use acetaminophen (Tylenol) instead.
3. Maintain hydration with at least 2 liters of water per day, particularly important during sports to prevent dehydration.
4. Maintain healthy diet and continue active lifestyle.
5. Follow-up with primary care physician or adult nephrologist closer to home; does not need to return to this clinic.
6. Call if symptoms worsen or with any additional questions.
